title: Heterogeneous Treatment Effects & Uplift Modeling
interviewAnswer: Heterogeneous treatment-effect models estimate how intervention effects differ across units. The target is incremental impact, not outcome probability, so ordinary response prediction can rank the wrong people.
keyPoints: CATE/uplift differs from propensity to respond.
Evaluate policy value and uplift curves carefully.
why: Heterogeneous Treatment Effects & Uplift Modeling appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: CATE/uplift differs from propensity to respond.
deepDive: Heterogeneous treatment-effect models estimate how intervention effects differ across units. The target is incremental impact, not outcome probability, so ordinary response prediction can rank the wrong people. Use randomized/identified treatment data. Evaluate policy value and uplift curves carefully. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Target retention offers to users who are likely to stay because of the offer, not users who would stay anyway.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Heterogeneous Treatment Effects & Uplift Modeling make?
How would you validate or debug Heterogeneous Treatment Effects & Uplift Modeling in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
